title: BMI and the planned publishing company with Jelly Roll
summary: In the late 1930s BMI courted the Spikes catalog but they stayed with ASCAP; Spikes and Jelly Roll planned a new publishing firm until Jelly Roll died.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: in about '38 or in '39, I think it was, the BMI Music Association was opening up to try to be like ASCAP, and they sent for us, and we went out there and they wanted us to come in with them 'cause we had a catalog, you know. They didn't have nobody with any catalog of music so we told them no, we was belonged to the ASCAP, and about ...we was going to--Jelly Roll and I--because my brother was blind and out of the business then, you know, and Jelly Roll and I was getting ready to open up a music publishing, and he died. That was about '38, I think it was, and that ended that.*
